I'm partial to Cicero's argument from chapter 6 of Stoic Paradoxes:

For whom are we to understand to be a rich man? To what kind of a man do we apply the term? To the man as I suppose, whose possessions are such that he may be well contented to live liberally, who has no desire, no hankering after, no wish for more.
[...]
the amount of wealth is not defined by the valuation of the census, but by habit and mode of life; not to be greedy is wealth; not to be extravagant is revenue. Above all things, to be content with what we possess is the greatest and most secure of riches.

If you make $20,000/year and you feel you have everything you need materially, you're rich. If you make $1,000,000/year and you desperately wish you had a bigger house, more sports cars, etc., you're poor.

By definition, someone who needs more is "needy" and it doesn't make sense that someone could be rich and needy at the same time.

Then following that train of thought, your current financial status would be the minimum amount of wealth for you to classify as rich then assuming that you are currently satisfied with your situation.
This is pretty philisophical, and I agree to a degree, but I think we're just discussing material wealth here.

What I like about the argument is that it actually is about material wealth. Cicero's not saying material wealth is insignificant compared to some sort of figurative wealth like being loved by friends and family. He's strictly talking about money and things that are worth money and concluding that being rich is having everything you want. The person who has insatiable material desires will never be rich because they will never feel they have enough.

I should also add that he's not arguing having more money is a bad thing. His definition allows for the possibility that a billionaire could be rich. It depends on whether that person feels satisfied with their financial situation.

Luminus had done well in his fight against Manius (https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/792098). Cruxius was not surprised. Even with only the slightest aid, these Spectra were quite the specimen. Created out of madness, blessed by The Deep, these creatures were a work of art.

But they were not strong enough for what Cruxius had planned.

Luminus felt his mind wander, and as it did so, so, too, did his form. It was not a pleasant feeling, knowing that your existence relied solely on your force of will, but Luminus was strong, stronger than most Spectra. It was odd that his mind would wander so...

A man suddenly stood before him, lounging against the frame of his door as if he had always been. He ate berries the like Luminus had never seen before, and he seemed to enjoy throwing them in the air before he caught them in his teeth. Luminus reacted out of instinct and attempted to probe the mind of the man who had suddenly appeared before him and found...nothing.

Then the man was in front of him. Had he moved? No! He simply was and then was not, then was again before Luminus could react. For the first time in his existence, Luminus very nearly lost his form. The man reached out and touched Luminus. As if Luminus were a corporeal thing, he could feel the man's touch, and he could not escape his grasp. The man reached into his pocket and pulled out a vine, whereon grew more of the berries Luminus saw the man eat. Luminus wanted to escape, wanted to fight, wanted to scream, but he couldn't focus on anything more than maintaining his own existence. His mind was muddled, full of uncertainty. Who was this man? What was happening to Luminus? Were the gods displeased?

The man thrust his hand into Luminus chest, and grabbed both vines together in his hand. The man never wavered. His gaze held Luminus in a way that could not be natural. "I will die here," Luminus thought to himself. Luminus could feel the man's hand on his vine. He could feel the thorns of the man's vine digging into his own. And then the man released him.

Luminus' thoughts suddenly cleared. He could feel the weight of uncertainty wash over him, and slough off, like oil on water. He could feel that his form was maintained, though he no longer focused on the act. It was as if his mind was now free; his form, established in his own subconscious.

"Gaze upon me, Luminus, and know me," Cruxius commanded. "You now hold in your form a piece of my domain, that which is made of uncertainty and hesitation, grown within the Crossroads that is my home. I have seen your actions, and they please me. You fight with guile and cunning, traits I value highly in my ranks. The vine you now bear is the mark of my favour. With this Primrose vine, I grant you greater power over your foes' mind than any in Gaea has ever known. You will walk as shadows in the night, and those that gaze upon you will forget that they have done so the moment their eyes leave your form, should you wish to remain hidden from them.[M] (For any Dr. Who fans, think: The Silence) [/M] They will retain your...suggestion, should you impart them with some command, and will feel compelled to obey, even if they forget you. All Spectra who choose to join your new Order of Flux will have this power, though they will first need to undergo the rites as I have shown them to you, whence they will be cleansed of their uncertainty and hesitation, and whence their form, as yours is, will be imprinted upon their minds, so they might be free, in some sense, of the burden of their form. Should the Primrose detect within them a lack of resolve, or the slightest hesitation, it will consume them, as it would have consumed you had you been unworthy. The vine will bloom, just as it would outside your form, and you may use the berries or flowers as you wish; their removal will not cause harm to your kind. I will teach my followers, as I have promised those before you, the secrets of aqua anima, the essence of the berries, which will cure those who succumb to the effects of the Primrose, should you wish to cure them. This is my gift to you. Let all houses of the Order plant within them a single Primrose berry, that a tree may grow to sprout vines, whereon grow the berries and blossoms I so admire. Let them trim this fruiting tree, such that it will not outgrow its home in the temples, and let the symbol of the Order be thus:"

Cruxius waved his hand and an [image](http://i.imgur.com/vjx5rHh.jpg) appeared before Luminus, floating in the air. It wavered a moment, then floated to Luminus' wall, where it burned itself into the wood.

"Do this, Luminus, and your kind might yet survive the trials that await this ill-fated world."

Cruxius turned, this time, walking away as a mortal would. He walked towards back door of Luminus' home, and opened it. What stood beyond was not the clearing as Luminus knew it. Beyond was a forest, vast beyond his comprehension, filled with trees that Luminus knew must be the Primrose, and a golden road, so much more beautiful for the stark contrast of those deadly woods. Cruxius stepped through the door and glanced back at Luminus for a moment. "Prepare for battle, Luminus. Your people have come into a world of madness, through madness, and it is towards madness that they inevitably must go." With that, he closed the door behind him.

Luminus moved without hesitation, tearing open the door the very instant it closed behind Cruxius, but only saw the clearing before him.
